To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface antigens of cloned cells derived from the rat central nerve system are correlated with their electrophysiological and morphological characteristics.
we have developed a method to classify cells in the rat central nervous sysytem as either nerve or glial cells.

1) a large group of cloned cells from the rat central and peripheral nervous system have been classified as nerve, glial, fibroblastic or muscle cells; 2) nerve cells express a common surface antigen, and some express a second and third common antigen; 3) glial cells express two common surface antigens, and muscle cells express one common antigen; 4) nerve, glial and muscle cells express at least six surface antigens in common.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a search for cell type-specific surface components on cells of the central nervous system.
the development of a set of surface antigens that can be used for the classification of cells of the nervous system.
a correlation of cell type and cell surface antigens in a group of cloned rat cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antigens described here are not cell type-specific, but rather are cell class-specific.
nerve cells are characterized by the presence of the N1, N2 and N3 antigens, and glial cells by the presence of either the G1 or the G2 antigen.

the cell-specific surface antigens described in this paper can be used to distinguish between the major cell types of the nervous system, and that these cell types are distinguishable by their surface antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a large number of surface antigens on cells of the nervous system which are specific for cell type and which may be involved in cell recognition.
the cell-specific surface antigens N1, N2, N3, G1 and G1 are useful markers for distinguishing neuronal, glial, fibroblastic and muscle cells in culture.
the surface antigenic properties of the cloned cell lines are in good agreement with their electrophysiological properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cell-specific surface antigens in conjunction with other criteria can be a powerful tool in the classification of cells.
we have identified a set of cell-specific surface components which can be used in the future to study the lineage of cells during development of the nervous system.
we have been able to identify surface antigens which are specific for nerve, muscle and glia, and we have used these to identify the cell types in our cloned cell lines.
